title: Container Engineer
description:
About Supabase

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth. More than 9 million developers and 250,000+ customers now build on Supabase, and the majority of new databases on the platform are created by AI app builders — so the systems underneath have to stay reliable while they grow fast.

About the Role

Container Engineering (ConEng) owns the internal container platform that runs Supabase's multi-tenant, multi-region services — the managed Kubernetes platform that other engineering teams build and deploy on top of. We own cluster lifecycle and cluster classes, multi-cluster and multi-region topology, capacity, scheduling, isolation and runtime safety, the higher-level platform APIs, the Kubernetes deployment contract and Argo semantics, rollout primitives, and runtime configuration and secret injection.

Your job is to make the platform itself trustworthy, observable, and cheap to operate at scale — and to raise the reliability bar for everyone who depends on it. This is not a gatekeeper role. You'll make the reliable path the easy path: building the automation and platform APIs that let product teams run safely by default, instrumenting what we operate, and making sure that when something breaks we detect it and recover fast.

The work spans three strength areas:

Tooling & ecosystem — deep knowledge of the container and orchestration landscape (Kubernetes, containerd/OCI, the CNCF ecosystem) and a clear point of view on how to compose it.

Software engineering — designing and building the platform's automation, controllers, and internal tooling as production code, including solutions that don't come pre-shaped by an existing tool.

Operational / SRE practice — the discipline (SLOs, error budgets, incident response, ORRs) that runs the platform at scale as a predictable one.

We expect you to be genuinely deep in at least one of these, and many of our strongest candidates are deep in two (usually leaning toward one). Bringing real strength across all three is rare and exceptional — and even then, no one is equally strong in all three at once, so you'd focus where you're most needed at any given time. Different profiles are welcome here; tell us which of these is your center of gravity.

What You'll Be Responsible For

Regardless of the skill set, all team members carry a share of the team's on-call rota, responding to platform incidents and driving them to resolution and follow-up.

Platform reliability & operations

  • Define SLIs/SLOs and error budgets for the container platform itself, and build error-budget policies that actually gate platform changes.

  • Own the Operational Readiness Review (ORR) process for new platform capabilities and major changes.

  • Design and track metrics for platform uptime, and increase observability into the platform by capturing the right metrics, logs, and traces across the platform layers.

  • Drive the incident-to-improvement pipeline: facilitate blameless postmortems, connect findings to readiness gaps, spot repeat failure patterns, and push through systemic fixes.

Software engineering

  • Build and maintain the platform's automation, controllers, operators, and internal tooling — writing production code and shipping it, not just wiring together existing tools.

  • Design and implement the platform-side CI/CD and rollout primitives that speed up platform deployments while working within proper change and release management.

  • Implement and maintain security automation for the platform: intrusion detection, automated remediation, and patch management.

  • Identify and quantify operational toil, and build the automation that removes it rather than just documenting it.

  • Contribute to the platform's continual testing automation — the test suites and pipelines that validate platform releases are fit for purpose before they reach tenants.

Tooling, ecosystem & architecture

  • Act as a platform reliability and architecture expert — contribute to failure-mode analysis, dependency mapping, and resilience design for multi-tenant container workloads.

  • Evaluate and evolve the platform's tooling ecosystem (orchestration, runtime, networking, isolation, and observability stack) with a clear, opinionated view on trade-offs.

  • Improve system architecture to reduce infrastructure cost while balancing security, reliability, and performance across tenants.

  • Guide teams building on the platform to design sustainable on-call practices for their own services: alert quality, escalation paths, runbook coverage, and noise reduction.

You Might Be a Good Fit If You

  • Have 5+ years in platform engineering, container/Kubernetes platform operations, SRE, or production infrastructure, and have operated production systems at scale and carried on-call for them.

  • Are genuinely deep in at least one — ideally two — of the three strength areas below (and tell us which is your center of gravity):

  • Tooling & ecosystem — know the container/orchestration landscape well: Kubernetes, containerd and the OCI/CRI standards, and the surrounding CNCF ecosystem (e.g. Argo CD/Argo Rollouts for GitOps and progressive delivery; Cilium/eBPF networking and the Gateway API; Karpenter/KEDA-style autoscaling; and workload-isolation runtimes such as gVisor or Kata Containers). You reason about trade-offs rather than reaching for defaults.

  • Software engineering — write real production code (Go and/or a comparable systems language) and can build controllers, operators, and platform APIs — stepping back to the underlying problem and building the right solution when no off-the-shelf tool fits.

  • Operational / SRE practice — are fluent in SLOs, error budgets, and operational KPIs; have led incident response and blameless postmortems; and have driven down MTTD/MTTR for systems you operated.

  • Have worked with large-scale multi-tenant systems and understand isolation as a spectrum — from namespaces, RBAC, network policies, and resource quotas through to stronger primitives such as virtual clusters (e.g. vCluster) or VM-class runtimes.

  • Operate confidently on AWS (multiple accounts, IAM, VPC) and are comfortable with infrastructure-as-code (Pulumi preferred; Terraform/CDK also fine) and Kubernetes.

  • Script and automate to eliminate toil rather than absorb it.

  • Communicate clearly with both infrastructure specialists and product engineers, and thrive in async, globally distributed teams.

  • Are comfortable navigating ambiguity and iterating toward better systems over time.

Nice to Have

  • Experience building and operating a multi-tenant Kubernetes platform that internal teams deploy onto.

  • Familiarity with policy engines (Kyverno, or OPA/Gatekeeper) and cost-attribution tooling (OpenCost/Kubecost) for per-tenant chargeback/showback.

  • Experience with managed database platforms or Postgres.

  • Familiarity with OpenTelemetry, Prometheus/VictoriaMetrics, Grafana, or similar observability tooling.

What We Offer

  • Fully Remote

    We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

  • ESOP

    Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

  • Tech Allowance

    Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

  • Health Benefits

    Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.

  • Annual Off-Sites

    Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

  • Flexible Work

    We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

  • Professional Development

    Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

About the Team

Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

  • ~400 team members

  • 60+ countries

  • 20+ languages spoken

  • Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F)

  • 540,000+ community members

We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

title: Customer Reliability Engineer
description:
About Us

At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.

At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.

Available Location: Singapore

Why This Role Exists

Cloudflare built its reputation helping build a better Internet, defending millions of sites, giving away SSL and DDoS mitigation when the industry charged premium prices. In an acceleratingly dangerous world, the scope of that mission has changed. We are becoming something more: critical infrastructure. Banks run their payment rails on us. Governments run public services on us. Media companies depend on us during live events. Health systems depend on us to provide care. Reliability for these customers is no longer a feature of our product. It is a mission.

Serving that customer base demands a different operating model. Traditional support organizations route tickets. Traditional engineering organizations ship features. Neither alone is enough when the stakes are this high. We are pivoting to something different: a customer-facing engineering organization, directly engaged with our customers at scale. This is work a central dev team cannot do from the inside of the network.

The Customer Reliability Engineering function is the spine of that pivot. CRE is SRE applied outward, the same engineering discipline, applied to the reliability of the systems our customers run on Cloudflare. You are the engineer who owns the problems that matter most to the customers who matter most, and you contribute directly to our products and tooling, in partnership with Product Engineering, to hold that standard across the entire customer base.

The Role

CRE is a rapid response team and a proactive engineering team. You fix things at the edge as they come up, and you help build the product capabilities that identify customer issues before they become a crisis. Both modes are equally core.

Rapid response. When a customer issue surfaces that is high-severity, cross-layer and complex, you are the engineer who answers. You reproduce the defect, isolate the root cause across Cloudflare's infrastructure and the customer's stack, drive the fix with Product Engineering, and confirm resolution. You hold on-call for high-severity incidents as part of a global shift rotation.

Proactive engineering. When no fire is burning, you work with Product Engineering and our platform teams to build the capabilities that make the next fire cheaper or unnecessary: telemetry pipelines that correlate signals across the customer base, detectors that fire before a human notices, diagnostic tooling that scales across hundreds of customers, automation that reduces toil for Customer Support. Every incident you carry generates engineering output that reduces the cost of recurrence. The work compounds.

Cloudflare is building CRE as an AI-native function. You will work with and help build agents and tooling that pre-diagnose incidents, surface relevant logs and configuration, and propose fixes with cited evidence. Engineers who ship AI-assisted diagnostics are the ones defining this discipline.

What You Might Work On

Rapid response:

  • Own a Sev-1 incident where a large financial services customer sees asymmetric latency from a single POP. Trace it through BGP routing and origin configuration. Produce the fix upstream.
  • Diagnose a recurring WebSocket disconnect that a media customer has been fighting for weeks. Isolate it to a specific interaction between WAF and their origin load balancer. Drive the fix with Product Engineering.
  • Partner with a government customer's SRE team during an active DDoS event. Help them shape their Magic Transit and WAF configuration in real time.

Proactive engineering:

  • Build, with Product Engineering, a distributed tracing capability that correlates Cloudflare edge signals with customer origin metrics so a single query tells the story of a failing request end-to-end.
  • Ship a detector for a class of WAF false positives silently degrading several customers. Get it into production before the next renewal cycle.
  • Prototype an AI agent that takes a new customer case, pulls relevant logs and config, and proposes a root cause with linked evidence. Deploy it internally. Measure whether it makes engineers faster. Iterate.

Responsibilities

Rapid incident response and root cause analysis. Own the most complex, high-severity customer issues end-to-end, from first signal through confirmed resolution. Lead deep-dive debugging across the full stack: edge, network, DNS, transport, APIs, application, customer-side configuration. Reproduce defects, validate fixes with Engineering, and confirm customer-side resolution. Produce postmortems other engineers rely on. Hold on-call for high-severity incidents as part of a global rotation that includes weekends.

Proactive reliability engineering. Analyze support and telemetry signals across the customer base to find systemic risks before they become incidents. Contribute monitoring, detection, and diagnostic capability to the core product and the engineering systems that give Customer Support early visibility into customer-affecting issues. Define customer-facing reliability metrics (error rates, resolution times, repeat-contact rates) and drive measurable improvement. Write automation that reduces mean-time-to-detect and mean-time-to-resolve.

Cross-functional partnership. Manage the technical escalation lifecycle with clear ownership and timely communication. Partner with Product Engineering to drive fixes, workarounds, and configuration changes that address underlying gaps. Represent the customer reliability perspective in engineering syncs, incident reviews, and post-mortem processes.

Technical leadership and enablement. Raise the technical floor of Customer Support through pair-debugging, structured knowledge transfer, and shared tooling. Document diagnostic procedures and resolution patterns in runbooks, internal knowledge bases, and AI skills. Share insights from customer-facing incidents to improve product documentation and operational readiness.

Product and platform depth. Maintain deep, current expertise across Cloudflare's product portfolio: edge networking, DNS, CDN, WAF, DDoS mitigation, Zero Trust, Workers, and our developer platform. Anticipate customer impact from new releases and architecture changes. Serve as a go-to subject-matter expert in one or more domains.

Requirements

  • Minimum 5 years of hands-on experience in site reliability engineering, escalation engineering, systems engineering, or a comparable deeply technical support / operations role, with at least 2 years in customer-facing environments.
  • Strong foundation in networking and security:
    • TCP/IP fundamentals: OSI model, IPv4/IPv6 addressing, subnetting, routing, switching.
    • Core protocols: DNS, HTTP/S, TLS/SSL, SMTP, SNMP, NTP.
    • Routing protocols: BGP, OSPF, including path selection and route propagation.
    • Firewall concepts: stateful/stateless inspection, rule sets, NAT, ACLs.
    • VPN and encryption: IPSec, SSL/TLS tunnels, GRE.
    • Zero Trust architecture, network segmentation, modern security models.
  • Proficiency with observability and diagnostic tooling: packet capture and analysis (Wireshark, tcpdump), log aggregation (Kibana, Elasticsearch), metrics dashboards (Grafana), distributed tracing.
  • Strong scripting and automation skills (Bash, Python) with a track record of shipping tooling that improves reliability and reduces toil.
  • Experience with incident management, postmortem culture, and SLO/SLI-based reliability practices.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication. Able to convey complex technical information clearly to engineers, leadership, and customers.
  • Comfort owning ambiguous, cross-layer problems. Composure under pressure during high-severity incidents.

Desired Skills & Experience

  • SRE, DevOps, or platform engineering experience with direct customer-facing accountability.
  • Deep expertise at both L3/L4 (network infrastructure) and L7 (application protocols, DNS, HTTP, WebSocket).
  • Expert-level proficiency with Linux command-line tools: curl, dig, git, traceroute, mtr, strace, ss.
  • Data-at-scale analysis using SQL, PromQL, or equivalent.
  • Familiarity with CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, Pulumi), and container orchestration (Kubernetes, Docker).
  • Track record of building internal tooling or diagnostic utilities that measurably improved team efficiency.
  • Demonstrated technical leadership: mentoring engineers, driving cross-team initiatives, influencing outcomes without direct authority.
  • Experience applying AI/ML to production engineering or operational workflows.
  • Comfort engaging directly with enterprise customer engineering teams, including on calls during incidents.

Bonus Points

  • Active Cloudflare user who understands the platform as a practitioner.
  • Hands-on experience with Workers, Pages, R2, D1, or other developer platform services.
  • Cloud networking and security experience across AWS, Azure, or GCP.
  • Web programming (HTML, JavaScript) and regular expressions.
  • Chaos engineering or formal reliability frameworks (e.g., Google SRE principles).
  • Managing or configuring non-HTTP services: email, DNS authoritative/recursive, FTP, SSH.

What Makes Cloudflare Special?

We’re not just a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company. We’re a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company with a soul. Fundamental to our mission to help build a better Internet is protecting the free and open Internet.

Project Galileo: Since 2014, we've equipped more than 2,400 journalism and civil society organizations in 111 countries with powerful tools to defend themselves against attacks that would otherwise censor their work, technology already used by Cloudflare’s enterprise customers--at no cost.

Athenian Project: In 2017, we created the Athenian Project to ensure that state and local governments have the highest level of protection and reliability for free, so that their constituents have access to election information and voter registration. Since the project, we've provided services to more than 425 local government election websites in 33 states.

1.1.1.1: We released1.1.1.1 to help fix the foundation of the Internet by building a faster, more secure and privacy-centric public DNS resolver. This is available publicly for everyone to use - it is the first consumer-focused service Cloudflare has ever released. Here’s the deal - we don’t store client IP addresses never, ever. We will continue to abide by our privacy commitment and ensure that no user data is sold to advertisers or used to target consumers.

Sound like something you’d like to be a part of? We’d love to hear from you!

Emerging Technologies & Incubation (ETI) is where new and bold products are built and released within Cloudflare. Cloudflare’s edge and network make it possible to solve problems at massive scale and efficiency which would be impossible for almost any other organization.

  • You will own your code from inception to release and bring attention to detail to the work you complete for both coding patterns & visual aesthetics.

About the Role

The Cloudflare Hyperdrive team builds the technology that makes regional databases feel like they are global. Hyperdrive is a core piece of the Cloudflare Developer Platform that accelerates database queries from Cloudflare Workers by pooling connections and caching data at the edge. By eliminating the massive latency overhead of TCP, TLS, and database-specific handshakes, Hyperdrive allows developers to use the databases they already know and love—like PostgreSQL and MySQL—without the "cold start" performance penalties typically associated with serverless environments.

Responsibilities

Hyperdrive is integrated directly into the Cloudflare global network and features:

  • Global Connection Pooling: Maintains "warm" connections to origin databases across the globe, reducing connection times by up to 90%.
  • Intelligent Query Caching: Automatically caches frequently run read queries as close to the user as possible.
  • Protocol-Aware Proxying: Features custom-built implementations of database wire protocols (PostgreSQL and MySQL) to parse and optimize traffic in real-time.
  • Seamless Integration: Works with existing ORMs and drivers, providing a simple connection string that "just works" for developers.
  • The team is geographically distributed across North America.
  • You will own your code from inception to release, delivering solutions at all layers of the software stack to empower Cloudflare customers. On any given day, you might write a design document that outlines how you plan to solve a specific problem, or fix a bug in how our user experience renders. You can expect to interact with a variety of languages and technologies including, but not limited to Rust, Go, C++, Typescript.

Desirable Skills, Knowledge, and Experience

  • You have 5+ years of professional experience with Rust, Go, or C++. You understand how to write code that respects CPU and memory constraints.
  • You are comfortable with the Linux networking stack. You know your way around TCP/IP, TLS, and WebSockets.
  • You don’t just use databases; you understand how they work. You’re familiar with connection lifecycles, transaction states, and wire protocols.
  • You enjoy the challenge of debugging complex, distributed systems and building for "five nines" reliability.

Bonus Points

  • Experience with PgBouncer, ProxySQL, or custom database middleware.
  • Familiarity with the Cloudflare Workers ecosystem and the unique stateful connection challenges of ephemeral computing.
  • You’ve contributed to database drivers, ORMs, or low-level networking libraries.
  • Experience using eBPF, perf, or other profiling tools to find and kill bottlenecks.

About the Role

AI inference is becoming core infrastructure. Every serious application will need access to many models, across many providers, with reliability, observability, security, cost control, and routing built in from the start. AI Gateway is Cloudflare’s bet that this layer should exist at the network edge: close to users, close to compute, and simple enough that a developer can adopt it with one API change.

We are looking for a Senior Systems Engineer to help build that layer. This is a deeply hands-on individual contributor role for someone who can move from a half-formed product idea to a working, production-ready system quickly. You will work across the stack — from distributed systems and high-throughput APIs to developer-facing workflows, dashboards, SDKs, and docs — helping define how developers build and operate AI applications on Cloudflare.

You should be excited by the current pace of the AI ecosystem. Provider APIs change weekly, new models appear constantly, and developer expectations are rising just as quickly. AI Gateway needs engineers who can build durable infrastructure in that environment without slowing down.

We also believe AI should change how we build software, not just what we build. We dogfood AI Gateway, Workers AI, and Cloudflare’s broader agent stack heavily. You should be comfortable using AI-native tools, agents, harnesses, and automation to improve your own engineering loop — and interested in building the internal tools and context that help a small team ship like a much larger one.

Responsibilities

  • Build core AI Gateway systems that handle high-volume inference traffic across providers, models, and Cloudflare’s global network.
  • Design and implement APIs, routing primitives, observability features, controls, and developer workflows that make AI Gateway reliable and easy to adopt.
  • Work across product and infrastructure boundaries with Workers AI, Agents, and the broader Developer Platform organization to make Cloudflare’s AI platform feel like one coherent product.
  • Turn ambiguous product and technical ideas into prototypes, design docs, shipped features, and measurable production improvements.
  • Improve reliability, performance, cost efficiency, and debuggability for latency-sensitive AI workloads.
  • Build the software — and the software that builds the software: agents, tests, harnesses, evaluation loops, operational tools, and internal context that help the team move faster with confidence.
  • Sweat the developer experience. Error messages, SDKs, dashboard flows, docs, examples, and API details all matter.
  • Mentor other engineers through design review, code review, debugging, and technical leadership without needing people-management authority.
  • Bring strong opinions, clear judgment, and a willingness to revise your view when data, users, or production reality prove otherwise.

Desirable Skills, Knowledge & Experience

  • 5+ years of experience building and operating production systems, ideally in AI infrastructure, developer platforms, cloud infrastructure, edge/proxy systems, high-scale APIs, or distributed systems.
  • Strong systems engineering fundamentals: networking, APIs, reliability, observability, data modeling, performance, and operational tradeoffs.
  • Experience designing or scaling distributed systems where latency, throughput, availability, and correctness all matter.
  • Ability to work comfortably across the stack, from API design and product surfaces to backend services, queues, storage systems, control planes, or performance-critical code.
  • Strong developer tools taste. You have used and built enough APIs, SDKs, dashboards, CLIs, docs, and internal platforms to know what makes them delightful or painful.
  • Clear technical communication: you can write design docs, explain tradeoffs, review architecture, and align engineers and product partners around a practical path forward.
  • A builder’s bias toward working software. You can prototype quickly, ship incrementally, and improve systems while they are already in production.
  • Operational judgment. You understand that at Cloudflare scale, rare bugs are not rare for long, and you build systems that are observable, resilient, and recoverable.
  • Comfort using AI-native development workflows and curiosity about how agents, tools, and automation can improve engineering productivity.

Bonus Points

  • Experience building AI/ML infrastructure, inference platforms, model gateways, LLM-powered applications, or provider abstraction layers.
  • Experience building developer-facing APIs, SDKs, CLIs, dashboards, or platform products at scale.
  • Hands-on experience with proxy, edge, gateway, routing, or traffic management systems.
  • Familiarity with the current AI ecosystem: model providers, model capabilities, agent frameworks, inference patterns, and the rough edges developers hit in practice.
  • Experience with cost controls, rate limits, caching, retries, fallbacks, evaluation, or observability for AI workloads.
  • Experience with TypeScript, Go, Rust, or similar systems/backend languages.
  • You have built or heavily customized your own agentic development environment: custom agents, harnesses, tools, or workflows that changed how you ship.
  • You have built something with AI Gateway, Workers AI, or a competing product, and have opinions about what is missing.
  • A track record of writing publicly about developer tools, infrastructure, systems, or AI products you have built.

When a customer or application talks to R2, they talk to the systems we build and operate.

R2 is growing rapidly, and the gateway must evolve to keep pace. The team is responsible for the API surface that handles authentication, request routing, rate limiting, and coordination between clients and R2's storage and metadata layers — all while maintaining strict compatibility with the S3 API and delivering low-latency, highly available access at global scale.

  • Own the request path end to end — authentication, authorization, routing, rate limiting, and error handling — and the interfaces between the gateway and R2's storage and metadata layers.
  • Own projects end to end: from design docs through implementation, testing, deployment, and production monitoring.
  • Continuously improve the reliability, performance, and observability of the gateway; ramp quickly into unfamiliar and legacy code paths and reduce operational toil.
  • Participate in on-call rotations, drive incident resolution, and write postmortems that raise reliability standards.
  • Use AI tools extensively to accelerate development, debugging, and operational tasks. We expect engineers to leverage AI as a core part of their workflow.
  • Collaborate across teams (storage infrastructure, metadata, networking, other platform teams) to coordinate API contracts, capacity planning, and cross-cutting initiatives.

  • Understanding of reliability and observability practices: monitoring, alerting, performance tuning, and incident response.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills; ability to explain technical decisions clearly and coordinate across teams.

title: Data API Engineer
description:
About Supabase

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Data API Engineer to join our Data API Team and help improve the feature set, reliability and performance of our Data API, based on the PostgREST project.

This role is ideal for someone who thrives in async, fast-paced environments and is excited about building developer tools that scale to millions.

What You’ll Be Responsible For

  • Work on PostgREST’s PostgreSQL driver (based on Hasql) and remove bottlenecks and improve it’s performance.

  • Work on PostgREST development of new features and bug fixes, aligned towards the goal of a multitenant Data API.

  • Resolve incidents and escalated support issues, while also improving observability and performance.

  • Collaborate cross-functionally with other teams to debug and solve integration issues with the Supabase platform.

You Might Be a Good Fit If You

  • Strong Haskell skills with at least 3 years of experience.

  • Experience using the C language.

  • Solid knowledge of SQL and plpgsql scripting in PostgreSQL.

  • Strong track record of contributing to and engaging with open-source projects. Bonus points if you’ve maintained an open source project.

  • Strong experience with providing technical support to users with varying levels of technical expertise.

  • Experience with debugging applications under the Linux operating system.

What We Offer

  • Fully Remote

    We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

  • ESOP

    Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

  • Tech Allowance

    Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

  • Health Benefits

    Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.

  • Annual Off-Sites

    Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

  • Flexible Work

    We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

  • Professional Development

    Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

About the Team

Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

  • ~400 team members

  • 60+ countries

  • 20+ languages spoken

  • Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F)

  • 540,000+ community members

We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

title: TPU Performance Engineer
region: San Francisco, CA / New York City, NY / Seattle, WA
description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the Role

As a TPU Performance Engineer, you'll be responsible for identifying and addressing performance issues across many different ML systems, including research, training, and inference. A significant portion of this work will involve designing and optimizing kernels for the TPU. You will also provide feedback to researchers about how model changes impact performance. Strong candidates will have a track record of solving large-scale systems problems and low-level optimization.

You may be a good fit if you:

  • Have significant experience optimizing ML systems for TPUs, GPUs, or other accelerators
  • Are results-oriented, with a bias towards flexibility and impact
  • Pick up slack, even if it goes outside your job description
  • Enjoy pair programming (we love to pair!)
  • Want to learn more about machine learning research
  • Care about the societal impacts of your work

Strong candidates may also have experience with:

  • High performance, large-scale ML systems
  • Designing and implementing kernels for TPUs or other ML accelerators
  • Understanding accelerators at a deep level, e.g. a background in computer architecture
  • ML framework internals
  • Language modeling with transformers

Representative projects:

  • Implement low-latency, high-throughput sampling for large language models
  • Adapt existing models for low-precision inference
  • Build quantitative models of system performance
  • Design and implement custom collective communication algorithms
  • Debug kernel performance at the assembly level

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$280,000—$850,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

description:
About Us

At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.

At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.

Available Locations

  • Austin, US

About the Role

Cloudflare built its reputation helping build a better Internet, defending millions of sites, giving away SSL and DDoS mitigation when the industry charged premium prices. In an acceleratingly dangerous world, the scope of that mission has changed. We are becoming something more: critical infrastructure. Banks run their payment rails on us. Governments run public services on us. Media companies depend on us during live events. Health systems depend on us to provide care. Reliability for these customers is no longer a feature of our product. It is a mission.

Serving that customer base demands a different operating model. Traditional support organizations route tickets. Traditional engineering organizations ship features. Neither alone is enough when the stakes are this high. We are pivoting to something different: a customer-facing engineering organization, directly engaged with our customers at scale. This is work a central dev team cannot do from the inside of the network.

The Customer Reliability Engineering function is the spine of that pivot. CRE is SRE applied outward, the same engineering discipline, applied to the reliability of the systems our customers run on Cloudflare. You are the engineer who owns the problems that matter most to the customers who matter most, and you contribute directly to our products and tooling, in partnership with Product Engineering, to hold that standard across the entire customer base.

CRE is a rapid response team and a proactive engineering team. You fix things at the edge as they come up, and you help build the product capabilities that identify customer issues before they become a crisis. Both modes are equally core.

Rapid response. When a customer issue surfaces that is high-severity, cross-layer and complex, you are the engineer who answers. You reproduce the defect, isolate the root cause across Cloudflare's infrastructure and the customer's stack, drive the fix with Product Engineering, and confirm resolution. You hold on-call for high-severity incidents as part of a global shift rotation.

Proactive engineering. When no fire is burning, you work with Product Engineering and our platform teams to build the capabilities that make the next fire cheaper or unnecessary: telemetry pipelines that correlate signals across the customer base, detectors that fire before a human notices, diagnostic tooling that scales across hundreds of customers, automation that reduces toil for Customer Support. Every incident you carry generates engineering output that reduces the cost of recurrence. The work compounds.

Cloudflare is building CRE as an AI-native function. You will work with and help build agents and tooling that pre-diagnose incidents, surface relevant logs and configuration, and propose fixes with cited evidence. Engineers who ship AI-assisted diagnostics are the ones defining this discipline.

Responsibilities

Rapid response:

  • Own a Sev-1 incident where a large financial services customer sees asymmetric latency from a single POP. Trace it through BGP routing and origin configuration. Produce the fix upstream.
  • Diagnose a recurring WebSocket disconnect that a media customer has been fighting for weeks. Isolate it to a specific interaction between WAF and their origin load balancer. Drive the fix with Product Engineering.
  • Partner with a government customer's SRE team during an active DDoS event. Help them shape their Magic Transit and WAF configuration in real time.

Proactive engineering:

  • Build, with Product Engineering, a distributed tracing capability that correlates Cloudflare edge signals with customer origin metrics so a single query tells the story of a failing request end-to-end.
  • Ship a detector for a class of WAF false positives silently degrading several customers. Get it into production before the next renewal cycle.
  • Prototype an AI agent that takes a new customer case, pulls relevant logs and config, and proposes a root cause with linked evidence. Deploy it internally. Measure whether it makes engineers faster. Iterate.
  • Rapid incident response and root cause analysis. Own the most complex, high-severity customer issues end-to-end, from first signal through confirmed resolution. Lead deep-dive debugging across the full stack: edge, network, DNS, transport, APIs, application, customer-side configuration. Reproduce defects, validate fixes with Engineering, and confirm customer-side resolution. Produce postmortems other engineers rely on. Hold on-call for high-severity incidents as part of a global rotation that includes weekends.
  • Proactive reliability engineering. Analyze support and telemetry signals across the customer base to find systemic risks before they become incidents. Contribute monitoring, detection, and diagnostic capability to the core product and the engineering systems that give Customer Support early visibility into customer-affecting issues. Define customer-facing reliability metrics (error rates, resolution times, repeat-contact rates) and drive measurable improvement. Write automation that reduces mean-time-to-detect and mean-time-to-resolve.
  • Cross-functional partnership. Manage the technical escalation lifecycle with clear ownership and timely communication. Partner with Product Engineering to drive fixes, workarounds, and configuration changes that address underlying gaps. Represent the customer reliability perspective in engineering syncs, incident reviews, and post-mortem processes.
  • Technical leadership and enablement. Raise the technical floor of Customer Support through pair-debugging, structured knowledge transfer, and shared tooling. Document diagnostic procedures and resolution patterns in runbooks, internal knowledge bases, and AI skills. Share insights from customer-facing incidents to improve product documentation and operational readiness.
  • Product and platform depth. Maintain deep, current expertise across Cloudflare's product portfolio: edge networking, DNS, CDN, WAF, DDoS mitigation, Zero Trust, Workers, and our developer platform. Anticipate customer impact from new releases and architecture changes. Serve as a go-to subject-matter expert in one or more domains.

Desirable Skills, Knowledge, and Experience

  • Minimum 5 years of hands-on experience in site reliability engineering, escalation engineering, systems engineering, or a comparable deeply technical support / operations role, with at least 2 years in customer-facing environments.
  • Strong foundation in networking and security:
    • TCP/IP fundamentals: OSI model, IPv4/IPv6 addressing, subnetting, routing, switching.
    • Core protocols: DNS, HTTP/S, TLS/SSL, SMTP, SNMP, NTP.
    • Routing protocols: BGP, OSPF, including path selection and route propagation.
    • Firewall concepts: stateful/stateless inspection, rule sets, NAT, ACLs.
    • VPN and encryption: IPSec, SSL/TLS tunnels, GRE.
    • Zero Trust architecture, network segmentation, modern security models.
  • Proficiency with observability and diagnostic tooling: packet capture and analysis (Wireshark, tcpdump), log aggregation (Kibana, Elasticsearch), metrics dashboards (Grafana), distributed tracing.
  • Strong scripting and automation skills (Bash, Python) with a track record of shipping tooling that improves reliability and reduces toil.
  • Experience with incident management, postmortem culture, and SLO/SLI-based reliability practices.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication. Able to convey complex technical information clearly to engineers, leadership, and customers.
  • Comfort owning ambiguous, cross-layer problems. Composure under pressure during high-severity incidents.
  • SRE, DevOps, or platform engineering experience with direct customer-facing accountability.
  • Deep expertise at both L3/L4 (network infrastructure) and L7 (application protocols, DNS, HTTP, WebSocket).
  • Expert-level proficiency with Linux command-line tools: curl, dig, git, traceroute, mtr, strace, ss.
  • Data-at-scale analysis using SQL, PromQL, or equivalent.
  • Familiarity with CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, Pulumi), and container orchestration (Kubernetes, Docker).
  • Track record of building internal tooling or diagnostic utilities that measurably improved team efficiency.
  • Demonstrated technical leadership: mentoring engineers, driving cross-team initiatives, influencing outcomes without direct authority.
  • Experience applying AI/ML to production engineering or operational workflows.
  • Comfort engaging directly with enterprise customer engineering teams, including on calls during incidents.

Bonus Points

  • Hands-on experience with Workers, Pages, R2, D1, or other developer platform services.
  • Cloud networking and security experience across AWS, Azure, or GCP.
  • Web programming (HTML, JavaScript) and regular expressions.
  • Chaos engineering or formal reliability frameworks (e.g., Google SRE principles).

description:

The IT System Operations Team provides engineering and operational expertise to the OpenAI IT organization. The team ensures that employee-facing systems, identity workflows, and enterprise applications operate in a predictable, governed, and continuously reliable manner as the organization scales.

The Enterprise Platforms pod runs the SaaS applications employees rely on to communicate, collaborate, and manage work. We’re looking for an IT Systems Engineer to join our Enterprise Platforms pod, with deep experience in platforms such as Google Workspace, Google Cloud Platform (GCP), and Slack, and a focus on application integration, automation, and internal tools. The goal is to reduce repeated manual administration and build reusable capability for user migrations, M&A integrations, and broader enterprise platform work.

You’ll pair that foundation with APIs and code to build integrations and tools, simplify administrative workflows, and turn recurring issues into durable engineering improvements.   • Have strong hands-on Terraform and infrastructure-as-code experience, including reusable modules, state management, resource imports, plan review, and automated validation and deployment. Write maintainable code and use APIs to extend automation across applications.

If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.

About the role

As a CE Specialist you will be the trusted technical advisor for customers adopting Cloudflare's network services. These include Magic Transit, Cloudflare WAN, Cloudflare Network Firewall and Cloudflare Network Interconnect (CNI), alongside Cloudflare One. You will lead Magic Transit and Cloudflare WAN POCs from design through to production cutover. You will also help customers modernize how they protect, connect and secure their networks and sites.

Responsibilities

  • Act as a trusted advisor, helping customers choose the right Cloudflare network and security solution for their business needs.
  • Lead qualified prospects through Solution Design and POC.
    • Magic Transit: plan and run POCs covering BGP onboarding, prefix advertisement, GRE/IPsec tunnels or CNI, and DDoS validation.
    • Cloudflare WAN: plan and run POCs covering site and branch connectivity (IPsec/GRE tunnels, CNI, Cloudflare One Appliance), data center and cloud-to-site connectivity, routing design, and coexistence with or migration from existing SD-WAN or MPLS.
  • Understand the customer's network topology, IP addressing, routing policy and security requirements. Then design an architecture that fits, including hybrid environments with Azure, AWS and GCP.
  • Run technical discovery, demos and workshops as part of the pre-sales cycle. Support RFP/RFI responses and technical validation.
  • Explain the benefits of Magic Transit, Cloudflare WAN and Cloudflare One compared with alternative approaches. These include traditional DDoS scrubbing services, appliance-based protection, SD-WAN solutions, next-generation firewalls and MPLS or traditional WAN.
  • Work with GTM partners to consistently achieve pipeline and revenue goals.
  • Present network and security transformation messages to senior technical leaders and executives.
  • Capture product and feature gaps and feed them back to Product and Engineering.

Core requirements

  • GTM experience: 5+ years in Customer Engineering, Pre-sales, Solutions or Systems Engineering, or Technical Sales. You should have experience guiding customers through discovery, solution design, POC and handover to delivery or support.
  • BGP and routing: Strong working knowledge of BGP (eBGP, route advertisement and filtering, AS paths, communities, anycast, RPKI and route hygiene). You should also be comfortable with static and dynamic routing, subnetting, route-based policy and split tunnels.
  • TCP/IP: Deep understanding of the TCP/IP protocol stack and packet-level troubleshooting (for example with tcpdump and Wireshark). This includes MTU/MSS, tunneling (GRE, IPsec), NAT and asymmetric routing.
  • DDoS protection: Understanding of L3/L4/L7 DDoS attack types and mitigation approaches (for example volumetric floods, SYN floods, amplification and reflection attacks). You should also understand how on-demand and always-on protection differ.
  • SD-WAN and WAN architecture: Familiarity with SD-WAN architectures and routing protocols (BGP and OSPF overlays), underlay and overlay design, local internet breakout, branch connectivity, and migration from MPLS or legacy WAN.
  • Fluent in English, written and spoken. Additional languages are a plus.
  • Ability to manage a project, work to deadlines and prioritize between competing goals.
  • Curiosity and learning agility. Cloudflare sits at the cutting edge of internet technology, so you are expected to keep up with industry trends as well as our own products.

Desirable skills

Network and security fundamentals

  • DNS: Good knowledge of DNS, including authoritative and recursive resolution, DNSSEC, DNS over HTTPS/TLS, DNS-based attacks (such as tunneling and cache poisoning) and DNS filtering.
  • Detailed understanding of the path from user to application, including hybrid and multi-cloud architectures (Azure, AWS, GCP).
  • Knowledge of end-user and application security risks. These include DDoS, malware, phishing, viruses, ransomware.
  • VPN and remote access challenges, and moving to Zero Trust access.
  • SIEM and log analytics platforms. You should also be comfortable with network telemetry such as NetFlow and sFlow.
  • Experience and knowledge with network and security vendors, including Cisco, Juniper, Fortinet, Palo Alto Networks, and Check Point (covering architecture, capabilities, configuration, and troubleshooting).

Market and competitive knowledge

  • Understanding of the market for CDN providers, Web Application Firewalls, remote access solutions, next-generation firewalls, CASB, DDoS mitigation, SD-WAN and secure gateway solutions.

Cloudflare One and Zero Trust

  • SASE concepts and Zero Trust networking architectures.
  • Knowledge of Cloudflare Zero Trust solutions: Access, Gateway, Browser Isolation, and WARP client deployment.
  • Secure Web Gateway, CASB and DLP.
  • IdP and authentication (SAML, OTP), plus SaaS application integration and tenant controls.
  • Client OS fundamentals and software distribution.

Compensation

  • For Portugal based hires: Estimated annual salary is between €59,000 - €92,000.

Equity

  • This role is eligible to participate in Cloudflare's equity plan.

What Makes Cloudflare Special?

We’re not just a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company. We’re a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company with a soul. Fundamental to our mission to help build a better Internet is protecting the free and open Internet.

Project Galileo: Since 2014, we've equipped more than 2,400 journalism and civil society organizations in 111 countries with powerful tools to defend themselves against attacks that would otherwise censor their work, technology already used by Cloudflare’s enterprise customers--at no cost.

Athenian Project: In 2017, we created the Athenian Project to ensure that state and local governments have the highest level of protection and reliability for free, so that their constituents have access to election information and voter registration. Since the project, we've provided services to more than 425 local government election websites in 33 states.

1.1.1.1: We released1.1.1.1 to help fix the foundation of the Internet by building a faster, more secure and privacy-centric public DNS resolver. This is available publicly for everyone to use - it is the first consumer-focused service Cloudflare has ever released. Here’s the deal - we don’t store client IP addresses never, ever. We will continue to abide by our privacy commitment and ensure that no user data is sold to advertisers or used to target consumers.

Sound like something you’d like to be a part of? We’d love to hear from you!

Please note that applicants who progress to the offer stage of the interview process may be asked to attend an in-person interview within one of the Cloudflare Offices or Cloudflare Hubs. More details about this will be available at that stage of the interview process.

This position may require access to information protected under U.S. export control laws, including the U.S. Export Administration Regulations. Please note that any offer of employment may be conditioned on your authorization to receive software or technology controlled under these U.S. export laws without sponsorship for an export license.

Cloudflare’s edge and network make it possible to solve problems at massive scale and efficiency which would be impossible for almost any other organization.

We build the infrastructure that makes the web Payable, powering the future of machine-to-machine commerce.

Here at Cloudflare, agentic commerce is a core part of our vision for the Agentic Internet. As AI agents increasingly navigate, consume, and act on the web, standard payment and authorization models built for humans are breaking down. We build tools that make the new internet payable by giving our users the ability to monetize access to their content, data, services, products, and outcomes across the Internet, regardless of where they are hosted.

Building these capabilities requires solving complex engineering problems across high-throughput web infrastructure, low-latency transaction processing, usage metering, outcome verification, digital wallets, and emerging agentic payment protocols (such as x402, WBA, ACP, and UCP). We bridge mainstream fiat commerce rails with decentralized protocols, enabling micro-payments at Internet scale.

We are a tight-knit group that communicates and collaborates regularly. We celebrate our achievements, support each other when we make mistakes, and hold each other and our work to a high standard.

In this role, you will define the architecture, build core systems, and establish technical standards powering machine-to-machine payments, metering, and monetization across Cloudflare's network.

As a Senior Engineer, your impact extends beyond individual features. You will shape product and engineering roadmaps by partnering directly with customers, product managers, and across Cloudflare teams. You will write architectural specs that guide engineers inside and outside the team, build systems that reduce complexity for others, and lead complex incident responses. You will be a prime reviewer for large systems, define core product KPIs, and mentor engineers across the organization to elevate our collective engineering practice.

What You'll Do

  • Design and build resilient, low-latency systems and core architectures that make web resources Payable for autonomous agents using emerging protocols (x402, WBA, ACP, UCP).
  • Write technical specs (RFCs) and architecture designs that encompass deliverables for developers both within the team and across other Cloudflare engineering groups.
  • Meet directly with customers and Product Management to clarify requirements, define actionable KPIs, and translate business needs into scalable architectural solutions.
  • Architect services to reduce code complexity for the team, ensure seamless recovery from internal and external failures, and improve overall system health observability.
  • Lead complex incident responses, retrospectives, and root-cause analyses while driving initiatives that proactively prevent customer escalations and reduce system alerts.
  • Debug and resolve high-complexity issues spanning multiple teams, services, and protocols, using these opportunities to teach others how to handle similar challenges.

title: Software Engineer, Identity Infrastructure
description:
About the Team

The Identity Infrastructure Engineering team builds the identity and access systems that OpenAI’s researchers, engineers, and internal teams rely on to protect critical systems and data.

We partner with Research, Applied Engineering, Infrastructure, IT, and Security to make secure access practical across cloud and internal environments.

About the Role

We’re looking for a hands-on software engineer to design and build high-scale, high-throughput secure access proxies and the distributed systems behind them. These are tier-zero services: researchers, engineers, and agents depend on them to reach critical infrastructure safely and reliably.

You’ll work at the intersection of networking, distributed systems, and infrastructure security, building the serving paths and control-plane integrations that connect identities to resources. Teleport is a core part of the current platform; the role also includes credential brokers, policy enforcement, and developer-facing integrations.

You’ll own the services you build from design and implementation through production. That means understanding human, agent, and workload traffic, improving throughput and tail latency, making authorization decisions auditable, and designing for safe multi-region rollout and recovery. We’re looking for someone who can turn a demanding security requirement into software that works well at scale and is straightforward for other engineers to use.

In this role, you will:

  • Design and implement secure access proxies, gateways, and credential brokers that provide narrowly scoped, auditable access to infrastructure and internal services while reducing standing privileges..

  • Integrate identity and access policy across clients, proxies, and target systems so approved permissions take effect promptly and access expires or is revoked when required. Ensure correct behavior when policy is stale or sessions remain active.

  • Build observability that explains the end-to-end access path: latency, errors, saturation, authorization decisions, and identity attribution, without leaking credentials.

  • Engineer safe multi-region rollouts, canaries, rollback, failover, and recovery. Validate changes with realistic test environments, load tests, and failure testing.

  • Keep core access services reliable, performant, and maintainable. Own production support, maintenance, upgrades, and incident recovery; ship durable fixes that reduce recurring failures, alert noise, and manual work.

  • Make secure access easy to adopt through reusable APIs, client tooling, diagnostics, and self-service workflows. Lead migrations that preserve critical workflows, with tested rollback and recovery paths and clear ownership across Infrastructure, Security, and SRE.

You might thrive in this role if you: 

  • Have built and operated production backend, proxy, networking, or infrastructure services with demanding scale or availability requirements.

  • Have practical networking depth and can reason about HTTP, TCP, TLS, DNS, routing, and load balancing across real request paths.

  • Can explain how you handled performance bottlenecks, partial failures, multi-region deployment, or a difficult production change in a system you personally built.

  • Understand authentication, authorization, least privilege, trust boundaries, credential handling, and the consequences of an access-control failure.

  • Have strong software engineering fundamentals and experience with Go, Rust, Python, or similar languages.

  • Use tests, profiling, telemetry, and reproducible experiments to debug across system boundaries and verify correctness, performance, and recovery.

  • Make practical scope decisions, communicate tradeoffs clearly, and follow through from code to production. Teleport or comparable access-platform experience is helpful; strong engineering and production ownership matter more than knowing every tool.

We make plugins easy to discover, install, and use, ensure they’re invoked at the right time, and help people find new ways to get value from them.

We want anyone to be able to turn a useful workflow into a plugin, share it, and have other people use it. A plugin can package instructions and skills with connections to the tools and data it needs. Our work spans creation and publishing, reliable execution across our products, clear permissions and approvals, and the controls admins need to bring plugins to their organizations. You’ll help shape what we build and how it works, translate user and developer needs into clear priorities, and guide technical decisions that balance rapid iteration with long-term reliability and maintainability.

title: Copywriter, Developer
region: San Francisco, CA / New York City, NY
description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

As a Copywriter, Developer at Anthropic, you will shape how our brand speaks to developers, an audience that is notoriously allergic to being marketed to and quick to spot anything that doesn't ring true. Developers who stay sharp, curious, and direct AI tools with their own judgment are the ones who will thrive, and your job is to help that idea land authentically rather than arrive as a slogan. You'll co-create a voice that developers recognize as empathetic, direct, and genuinely useful, and you'll bring that voice to every place our brand meets a developer.

In this role, you'll own the brand-led developer writing that sits between Dev Rel's technical content and pure marketing: launch narratives, campaign work, social, paid, event materials, and developer work that shows up in enterprise contexts. You'll partner closely with Dev Rel as an embedded extension of their team, co-own the developer voice and tone guide with Comms, work with Claude Code and developer marketing leadership on strategic initiatives, and sit within a developer creative pod alongside a brand designer and program manager, with our Head of Copy and Content as your craft lead.

Responsibilities

  • Own the developer-facing expression of brand campaigns, starting with Keep Thinking, translating brand-level ideas into writing that works across launches, social, and paid
  • Build the developer voice and tone guide in partnership with Comms and Dev Rel, then turn it into the templates and examples the creative team uses for developer work
  • Own the brand-led developer assets that sit between technical content and marketing, from event and campaign materials to developer writing in enterprise contexts
  • Partner daily with Dev Rel as an embedded extension of their team, complementing the technical content they own rather than duplicating it
  • Develop launch narratives and short-form copy that adapt expert, technical material into sharp, accurate writing developers trust
  • Lead copy for the developer creative pod, working side by side with brand design and program management to ship integrated work
  • Partner with Claude Code leadership and developer marketing leadership on strategic initiatives that shape how we show up for developers
  • Present work and a clear rationale for voice and craft decisions to stakeholders across Brand, Dev Rel, Comms, and marketing
  • Manage feedback from technical reviewers and Comms so that what ships is both accurate and within what we can say externally
  • Track how developer-facing work lands and use what you learn to sharpen the voice, the templates, and the work itself

You may be a good fit if you

description:

Every dollar Anthropic earns and every dollar it spends on compute has to reach the books correctly, and the volume grows with Claude usage. That data comes from across the company and from partners: usage and billing, compute, infrastructure assets, leases. Products and pricing models keep launching, and each one adds another path into the books. Our goal is a continuous close with zero material issues, with audit-grade controls.

You’ll build the platform that gets us there: one front door for every finance event, an append-only ledger, and an accounting engine that posts each event exactly once. This is a distributed systems problem with an unusually high correctness bar. The system has to be right to the cent, replay cleanly and explain any number as of any date, at that volume. You will shape its architecture. Its users include Claude agents, which read and write through the same APIs and controls as people.

You’ll work closely with SWEs in Billing, Compute and Infra on shared contracts and APIs, and with product owners, finance operations and internal audit to turn accounting and controls requirements into designs.   • Drive the build of the accounting ledger and engine: an append-only ledger with idempotent posting, a rules framework that turns business events into journal entries, translation into the ERP, and period locks

  • Experience designing relational data models and writing SQL for complex, versioned data
  • Experience designing APIs, SDKs and service-to-service integrations used by other teams
  • Experience building systems with auditability, access control or compliance requirements
  • Experience turning requirements from non-engineering partners into technical designs

  • Experience building with LLMs and agents, including MCP
  • Built a ledger, sub-ledger, billing or payments system

title: Capacity Engineer
description:
About Us

At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.

At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.

Available Locations: Austin, Texas

About the role

The Demand Planning team sits at the intersection of traffic forecasting, infrastructure strategy, and operational execution. We predict when, where, and how many servers to deploy across Cloudflare's global edge so that customers' traffic stays in-region and they never have to think about infrastructure. This is not a reporting role — it is a planning and engineering role that requires you to build the models, own the data, and translate forecasts into real deployment decisions.

As a Capacity Engineer, you will own one or more planning regions end-to-end with light supervision. That means maintaining the models, catching problems before they become incidents, working directly with hardware sourcing and infrastructure teams, and contributing to the data pipelines that feed your planning work. You will be the point of contact for your region — not someone who supports a more senior planner, but someone who runs the work.

This is a role for someone with 3-5 years of experience who is ready to operate with real ownership and is actively growing toward full autonomy. You will work alongside senior peers who set team-wide standards, and you will be expected to contribute to cross-regional consistency — not just execute within your own lane. You will also work fluently with AI tooling, including OpenCode AI and MAS agent workflows, as a normal part of how planning gets done on this team.

Why Cloudflare/ Why This Team

Cloudflare's network spans hundreds of cities and carries a meaningful fraction of global internet traffic — the planning decisions this team makes have direct consequences at that scale. - Work directly with hardware sourcing, DCS, and infrastructure teams to translate forecasts into actionable deployment plans

- Proactively identify capacity risks in your region and surface them before they require escalation

- Comfort working with large infrastructure datasets and translating them into decisions

- Clear written and verbal communication — you can explain a capacity recommendation to a finance partner or a network engineer without losing either of them

- Demonstrated ability to own a workstream end-to-end with light supervision

Athenian Project: In 2017, we created the Athenian Project to ensure that state and local governments have the highest level of protection and reliability for free, so that their constituents have access to election information and voter registration. Since the project, we've provided services to more than 425 local government election websites in 33 states.

  • Culture & Values: Model Cloudflare's values and build an inclusive, high-performance team culture rooted in curiosity, ownership, and continuous improvement.

You will further be responsible for the development and implementation of consistent processes and tools for consistent and effective management of our infrastructure. This is a highly visible position that requires deep technical understanding of datacenter infrastructure, physical and logical network configuration, system administration, server provisioning and troubleshooting, and basic experience with data analysis and project management.

To be successful in this position, you should have excellent technical skills, communication skills, and be able to navigate a range of challenges and constraints (e.g. schedule adherence, time zones, and cultures). You will have the opportunity to (literally) build a faster, safer Internet for our millions of users and the billions of web surfers that visit their sites each month.

Key responsibilities

  • Provisioning, monitoring and maintaining hardware, software, and network in new Cloudflare data centers.
  • Perform server administration tasks remotely using IPMI/BMC tools, including server provisioning, monitoring, troubleshooting and firmware updates.
  • Perform network configuration tasks to network devices in greenfield deployment and brownfield migration activities.
  • Managing remote contractors to complete datacenter installations and upgrades (rack and stack), including coordinating with hardware manufacturers, datacenter and network providers, logistics partners and other service providers in support of our 700+ growing datacenter locations.
  • Build automation to eliminate repetitive work using Python scripts and templated change management workflows (Python + Jinja-based) that standardize deployment steps. Our team also develops agentic AI tools to reduce admin overhead and handling other operational toil.
  • Planning and implementing network and server installations, including in the areas of facility power (AC/DC), cooling, security/access, rack layout and cable management.
  • Providing technical leadership and guidance to remote contractors and junior team members during deployment activities—walking them through configurations, troubleshooting steps, and quality checks.
  • Creating and maintaining documentation, plans, SOPs, MOPs and runbooks.
  • Collaborating with internal teams (Infrastructure Engineering and Planning, Network Engineering and SRE) on day-to-day operations and project planning.
  • Coordinating installation of cross-connects globally in support of physical network expansion.
  • Assisting with the definition, documentation and implementation of consistent processes and standardization across all regions.
  • Limited travel.
